ikh (ch: soft hiss, like a cat's hiss)
Old English had 'ic' for I. Say 'itch' with a hiss at the end: ich.
Old English 'thou' → du (th becomes d). Use it with friends, kids and family.
He → er. The R ending is the masculine marker, just like in deR.
she → sie. With a capital S (Sie) it becomes polite 'you', for strangers and your boss.
it's → es ist. It is also the weather subject: es regnet, it's raining.
we're → wir. German W sounds like English V.
Pointing at the whole group: 'Hey, all of YOU over here!' Ihr sounds like 'ear', so all of you, lend me your ears.
Like English 'one' or 'a man' with no face: man sagt = one says. One N = generic; der Mann (two N) = a real man.
The reflexive for he, she, it and they: er wäscht sich, he washes himself. Think 'self' squeezed into sich.
In English (via Yiddish) a 'mensch' is a decent person. Der Mensch: every human being.
man → Mann, with double N like two strong arms. Der Mann.
Frau Merkel = Mrs. Merkel. Hausfrau = housewife. Die Frau.
Kindergarten = children's garden. A kid is das Kind: neuter, too young for a gender.
Hamlet in German: 'Sein oder Nichtsein', to be or not to be. Ich bin, du bist, er ist (bin ≈ been, ist ≈ is).
have → haben (v becomes b). Ich habe ≈ I have.
Not 'word'! Think 'to turn into': es wird kalt, it's turning cold. Also builds the future: ich werde gehen, I will go.
can → ich kann. Same word, same job.
shall → ich soll. A duty someone else puts on you: Du sollst... = Thou shalt...
Ich will looks like 'I will' but means 'I WANT'. Your will is what you want, not the future.
say → sagen. A saga is a story that's told, said.
make → machen (k becomes ch). Was machst du? = What are you doing?
give → geben (v becomes b). Es gibt = there is / there are.
come → kommen. Komm her! = Come here!
go → gehen. Wie geht's? = How's it going?
see → sehen. Same verb, German just adds -hen.
wise / wisdom / wit → wissen. Ich weiß = I know. A wise person knows facts.
find → finden. Also used like 'I find that good' = I think it's good.
stand → stehen. St at the start sounds 'sht'.
He is standing at the door.
let → lassen. Also laissez-faire = let do. Lass mich! = Let me be!
Glue on your shoes: you're stuck, you have to stay, bleiben. Think 'bide' your time: the b-l-ei-b-en stays put.
Old English 'niman' (take), still in 'numb' (taken by cold) and 'nimble' (quick to take). Ich nehme das = I'll take that.
Ends in R like 'he' → er. Always blue in this app.
Ends in E like 'she' → sie. Every plural uses die too. Always red.
Ends in S like es (it). Also 'that': Was ist das? = What is that? Always green.
k + ein = 'not a'. Kein negates nouns; nicht negates the rest.
and → und (d sounds like t at the end).
or → oder. Ja oder nein? Yes or no?
'Ah, but...' The objection always starts with aber.
that → dass (th becomes d, t becomes ss). Two S = conjunction; one S (das) = article.
I know that you are here.
'Why are you running?' 'Because of that VILE smell!' Weil sends the verb to the end.
when → wenn. Works for 'if' and 'whenever'. Careful: 'when?' as a question is wann.
as → als: als Kind = as a child. Comparing: größer als = bigger than.
this → dies (th becomes d). Dieser Weg = this way.
up → auf (p becomes f). On top, up there. Also 'open': the shop is auf.
The book is on the table.
on / at → an. Touching the side: a picture an der Wand, on the wall.
The picture is hanging on the wall.
by → bei. Bei Oma = at Grandma's.
with ≈ mit. Shake hands with a mitt on: mit.
Otto VON Bismarck = Otto OF Bismarck. Also 'from' and possession: ein Freund von mir.
to → zu (t becomes z). Also 'too': zu viel = too much.
out → aus. Ich komme aus... = I come from... Also 'off': das Licht ist aus.
Hidden in 'neighbour' (nigh = near, nach = toward). Nach Berlin = to Berlin; nach dem Essen = after eating.
over → über. Your Uber flying over the city.
The plane flies over the city.
The cat is under the bed.
before / fore → vor. Forehead = the front of your head.
He is waiting in front of the house.
for → für. A gift: für dich, for you.
Around the clock face: um acht Uhr = at eight o'clock. Also 'around': um die Ecke.
Bis morgen! = Till tomorrow! Think 'bis' as a quick kiss goodbye: see you till then.
Knock knock: he's STILL at the door, noch knocking.
Like 'ever' with an M: forever and ever, immer.
'Hoy! Today is the day!' Heute starts with that shout.
einmal = once, zweimal = twice, like 'one meal, two meals'. Also softens commands: Komm mal!
Zeitgeist = spirit of the time. time → Zeit (t becomes z).
day → Tag (d becomes t). Guten Tag = good day.
end → Ende. Happy End is even a German word for a happy ending.
what → was (t becomes s). NOT 'was' in English.
'Wee! How fun!' Wie geht's? = How's it going?
there → da (th becomes d). Ich bin da = I'm here, I've arrived.
not / naught → nicht. Sein oder Nichtsein: to be or NOT to be.
yeah → ja. J sounds like Y.
English has no one-word answer for this: 'You're not coming?' 'Doch!' = 'Oh yes I am!'
You're not coming? Yes, I am!
You stub your toe and yell 'OUCH!' Your friend does too: auch!
'Nur, I'll have just one.' Picture a stingy waiter giving you only one fry.
so → so. Same word, same use.
Not 'also'! Also = 'so / well then'. 'Also... let's go.' For 'also' say auch.
'Sir, VERY good!' A German butler says sehr gut, sir. Goes before adjectives.
full / fill → viel. Viel Glück = lots of luck. Quantity, not intensity.
A goose swallowing a WHOLE watermelon: 'GANTS!' Ganz = whole, totally.
two / twin / twice → zwei (tw becomes zw).
gross (as in gross weight, big total) → groß. ß sounds like SS.
new → neu. Neuschwanstein = new swan stone castle.
house → Haus. Nach Hause = home(wards). Das Haus.
Related to 'stead' (homestead, a place). A city-state: die Stadt.
live → leben (v becomes b). A verb turned noun is das.
gold → Geld. Money used to be gold.
way → Weg. Der Weg. Also 'away': weg!
